I will not start from zero. I will start from what has worked for me here in Quzhou County and adjust a little for cost, water, and the crop’s earning power. With 6 mu and only 2 people at home, I do not want a plan that looks good on paper but is too heavy on labor. I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on 4 mu because that land use is steady, the machinery service is easy to find, and with well irrigation I can still protect yield in a dry spell. I will keep 2 mu in stevia because its return can be better than grain, but it needs cleaner field management and closer watching, so I will not expand it too much at my age. Because I have a high education level and many years in the field, I look at nutrient balance, not only habit. Wheat here responds clearly to nitrogen, but if I push nitrogen too hard and do not hold phosphorus and potassium, the stand gets greedy, lodging risk rises, and grain filling is not as stable. Maize is the same: I will feed it enough early and then topdress with water so I do not waste fertilizer. For stevia, I will hold nitrogen in a controlled range and give more potassium because leaf crop quality matters. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, but I still watch every yuan, so I will keep the rates close to last year and put money first into seed, fertilizer, irrigation, and a manageable number of pesticide sprays.
